title: Ethan's Answer
speaker: Ethan Valen, by letter
text: Ethan’s reply contains no ornaments. He will examine the evidence of your birth. If it stands, he offers to be Protector beside an adult monarch, with his powers written and limited. You would be uncle and nephew choosing a common government, rather than rivals repeating the damage of the previous generation.

choices.text: Accept. Let him be Protector if the proofs hold.

effects.text: Ethan and Arlo are suddenly a problem for everyone who wanted them apart.

choices.text: Tell him the crown is yours to try for, brother or not.
Ask him to wait until the papers are in a hall.

title: The Miller's Tithe
speaker: A miller
text: A miller says the tithe took his seed corn. The Flame says the tithe is holy. Your army says bread is holy too.

choices.text: Ease his tithe and eat the difference later.
Keep the tithe. Holiness can wait until the war is over.
Split it and please nobody completely.

title: The Relic Will Not Wait
speaker: A hearth priest
text: Aldren's priests want to carry the hearth-relic through a town that is already hungry. A procession feeds faith. It also blocks a road your grain needs.

choices.text: Let them pass and walk with them a mile.
Stop the procession. Roads are for carts.
Pay for a smaller rite at dusk.

title: A Royal Messenger in a Ditch
speaker: A road warden
text: He was carrying nothing you can use and wearing colours that make the ditch a political act. The nearest village swears it was bandits. The wounds are too careful.

choices.text: Investigate, and hang no one today.

effects.success_text: A ring points at a house.

success.text: A house seal was on the killer's pay.

fail.text: You spend the week learning how a man dies without a reason.

choices.text: Burn a barn and call it justice.
Bury him with honour and move the grain.

title: The Salt Has Gone
speaker: A quartermaster
text: Without salt the meat turns, and the coast knows it. Celene's ships have salt. They also have a price that includes a compliment you may not want to pay.

choices.text: Buy salt and swallow the compliment.
Seize a warehouse and call it necessity.
Let the meat turn. Teach the host to eat simpler.

title: A Bard Who Knows Too Many Verses
speaker: A bard
text: He will sing you as saviour, butcher, or bastard, depending on the purse. The verses are already written. Only the chorus is for sale.

choices.text: Pay for the kind chorus.
Pay him to sing nothing.
Have him whipped for the verse he has not sung yet.

title: The Armoury Leaks Spears
speaker: An armoury clerk
text: Spears are leaving the armoury at night. It may be theft, or it may be a sergeant arming his cousins. Both are reasons to be angry. Only one is a reason to be afraid.

choices.text: Audit it in daylight.
Hang the night watch and replace the lock.
Ignore it until the count is embarrassing.

title: A Widow at the Gate
speaker: A widow
text: Her husband died in a skirmish that will not make a song. She wants his pay, or his name said by someone with a banner. The pay is small. The precedent is not.

choices.text: Pay her, and the next widow who hears.
Say his name and give no coin.
Tell her war does not keep a pension list.

title: The Horses Are Sick
speaker: A farrier
text: A cough is moving through the horse lines. Maren riders would know what to do. Your farrier knows what it costs. Resting them slows every plan you had for the week.

choices.text: Rest them.

effects.text: The cavalry does not move this week.

choices.text: Work them anyway.
Send to Maren for a farrier and pay the pride.

title: Knives in a Tavern
speaker: A town watchman
text: Two of your soldiers and three townsmen discovered a political theory at the bottom of a cup. Someone is bleeding. If you hang a soldier you lose a spear. If you hang a townsman you lose a street.

choices.text: Punish your own and pay the town.
Punish the town and keep the spears.
Fine both and close the tavern for a week.

title: A Warrant with Your Seal
speaker: A tax farmer
text: Someone is collecting taxes with a seal that looks like yours and is not. The coin is going into a pocket that may belong to a rival, a clerk, or a joke that has become a crime.

choices.text: Hunt the seal.
Announce the warrants void and start again.
Take the credit and the coin, then stop the practice.

title: The Bridge Wants Timber
speaker: A bridge warden
text: The Dorn bridge will fail in the next hard rain. Repairing it helps whoever holds it, including you, including Alistair, including the grain. Leaving it is a strategy only if you enjoy swimming.

choices.text: Repair it.
Break it so no host crosses easily.
Leave it for the rain to decide.

title: Men with Counting Sticks
speaker: A clerk with a stick
text: A census will tell you who can pay and who can fight. It will also tell every village that you intend to use the answer. People hide sons from counting sticks.

choices.text: Count them.
Count grain, not sons.
Send the counters home.

title: The First Frosts Are Early
speaker: A granary clerk
text: The season turns before the barns do. You can buy, seize, or pray. Prayer is cheapest and has the worst record.

choices.text: Buy grain at a bad price.
Seize a tenth and call it a loan.
Ask the Flame to bless what you already have.

title: Pilgrims on the Hearth Road
speaker: A shrine keeper
text: They are walking to a shrine and they are eating your countryside as they go. Taxing pilgrims angers the Flame. Feeding them angers the quartermaster.

choices.text: Feed them one night.
Tax the road.
Divert them around your stores.

title: A Woman the Village Wants Burned
speaker: A village headman
text: They say she soured milk and spoke to a dead king. The Flame has not asked for a fire. The village has. You can be the person who stops a mob or the person who owns one.

choices.text: Stop it. Send her out of the village alive.
Give her to them.
Hold a dull trial and bore the mob into going home.

title: A Knight Without a House
speaker: A hedge knight
text: He has a horse, a grievance, and a desire to be seen kneeling to someone who might win. Taking him annoys the houses. Refusing him annoys the story you are telling about merit.

choices.text: Take his sword.
Send him to a house that can feed him.
Tell him the war is not a ladder.

title: Boys Who Want Spears
speaker: A sergeant
text: They are not men. They will be, if you arm them, or if someone less careful does. The villages call it theft. The sergeants call it the future.

choices.text: Send them home.
Train them and keep them off the front.
Put them where the line is thin.

title: A Cart That Did Not Arrive
speaker: A quartermaster
text: The grain was signed out and never signed in. Someone ate your week. Finding them is a use of soldiers. Replacing the cart is a use of gold.

choices.text: Replace it and punish no one yet.
Find the thieves.

effects.success_text: The cart is in a barn.
effects.fail_text: The barn is empty and angry.

choices.text: Cut rations and call it discipline.

title: Smugglers Who Know the Coves
speaker: A harbour master
text: They can move grain past tariffs, or they can move messages. Celene would rather you hanged them. Your spymaster would rather you hired them.

choices.text: Hire them.
Hang them for Celene's friendship.
Fine them and let them sail.

title: Bad Air in the Reach
speaker: A mine factor
text: A shaft in the north has killed four miners. Closing it saves lives and costs iron. Keeping it open is a number you can defend only if you never say it aloud.

choices.text: Close the shaft.
Keep it open and pay the widows.
Close it for a month and reopen when the air is tested.

title: Deserters with Another Banner
speaker: A picket
text: They left a rival's host and they will tell you its strength if you feed them. Feeding deserters teaches your own men that leaving is a career.

choices.text: Feed them and listen.

effects.text: You learn a rival's host is hungrier than it looks.

choices.text: Return them under a flag of truce.
Hang them as a lesson in both directions.

title: Talk of Fever in the Ports
speaker: A port clerk
text: It may be a fever and it may be a story merchants tell when they want the road closed. Closing the road protects you and starves a town. Leaving it open is a gamble with other people's bodies.

choices.text: Close the road.
Leave it open and send a physician's apprentice.
Buy their unsold grain cheap.

title: A Feast the Lords Expect
speaker: A steward
text: A supper has been promised and the stores have not. Cancelling insults the nobility. Holding it insults the quartermasters and, later, the soldiers.

choices.text: Hold it.
Cancel it and eat with the host.
Hold a thin supper and call it mourning.

title: Arms Under a Market Stall
speaker: A market reeve
text: Someone is selling spearheads that used to be yours. Smash the stall and you smash a street. Tax it and you admit the theft has become trade.

choices.text: Smash the stall.
Tax it.
Buy the heads back and ask no names.

title: The Price of Bread
text: Bread costs more than it did last week. You can rage at the bakers, subsidise the loaf, or let the price teach the city who is in charge.

choices.text: Subsidise the loaf.
Blame the bakers in public.
Leave the price alone.

title: A Sermon with Your Name in It
text: A priest is deciding, sentence by sentence, whether you are a scourge or a shelter. You can stand there, send a captain, or let the square finish without you.

choices.text: Stand in the square and be seen listening.
Send a captain to be seen instead.
Be elsewhere. Sermons do not require the subject.

title: The Host Is Hungry Tonight
text: The pots are thin. A captain wants permission to take a village's pigs. The village is close enough to hear the argument.

choices.text: No pigs. Tighten belts.
Buy the pigs.
Take them.

title: A Quarrel Between Companies
text: Two companies want the same dry ground. It is beneath you until one of them decides it is about your favour.

choices.text: Make them share and disappoint both captains.
Pick a favourite.
Move your own tent into the wet ground.

title: The Market Has a New Rumour
text: Today's rumour is already choosing a winner, and it is not always you. You can correct it, mock it, or add a worse one.

choices.text: Correct it, plainly.
Mock it and look untouchable.
Pay for a worse rumour about a rival.

title: The Levy Wants to Go Home
text: They were promised a month. The month is over. Keeping them builds the host and breaks the promise. Sending them home does the opposite.

choices.text: Keep them and call the promise a war.
Send the oldest home.
Pay them to stay another month.

title: The Night Watch Is Thin
text: You can walk it yourself, hire more eyes, or accept that some nights the camp is a rumour of safety.

choices.text: Walk it yourself.
Hire more eyes.
Accept the thinness.

title: A Caravan Asks for an Escort
text: Merchants will pay for spears they do not have to feed afterwards. The spears are the same ones you needed for a different road.

choices.text: Escort them.
Refuse. The host is not a guard company.
Tax them for the road and escort nothing.
